dek.text: Tesla's quarterly capacity table lists its Texas vehicle and Megapack rows as Production. The Texas row for Optimus, its humanoid robot, reads Construction.

introduction.text: [Tesla's update for the third quarter of 2026 was released for a webcast set for {{date:c1}}](c1). [Its table of installed annual manufacturing capacity lists Model Y in Texas at more than {{number:c2}} a year, with the status Production](c2). [The Cybertruck](c3) [and the Cybercab sit in the rows under the same Texas label at more than {{number:c4}} each, also Production](c4). [Megapack in Texas is listed at {{number:c5}} GWh](c5).

[One row is different. The Texas row for Optimus reads Construction and gives no capacity figure](c6). [Tesla defines construction as factory and infrastructure buildout plus tool installation](c11). [Optimus production began on high volume lines in Fremont](c27), [where the California row reads Early Ramp](c7).

sections.heading: The machines that train the software

paragraphs.text: [The supporting table lists Cortex 1 in Texas at more than {{number:c12:1}} MW of training compute](c12) [and Cortex 2, in the row under it, at more than {{number:c13:1}} MW](c13). [Tesla plans to reach {{number:c21}} MW by the end of the year](c21), [supporting both vehicle and humanoid robot autonomy software](c22). The update does not say where that compute will sit.

[Tesla says it kept building the Austin Fab during the quarter](c23) [and plans to start commissioning equipment there in {{number:c24}}](c24). [It also says it began production at Megafactory Texas](c25).

sections.heading: What a capacity figure is not

paragraphs.text: [A footnote to the tables says installed capacity is not the current production rate](c8). [Tesla says production rates depend on equipment uptime](c9), [component supply, downtime for factory upgrades, regulatory considerations and other factors](c10). [The update gives no count of Cybercabs built, deployed or carrying riders](c34).

[Tesla says it began putting the Cybercab into its Robotaxi fleet in Austin](c28). [NHTSA records that commercial deployment began with a small number of Cybercab vehicles in Austin on {{date:c39}}](c39). [The vehicles lack permanently attached conventional controls such as a brake pedal, a gas pedal, a steering wheel and mirrors](c42). [NHTSA opened an audit query into the process and data behind Tesla's certification of the car](c43), [and its resume still shows that query as open](c35).
